topicName: Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Ansible) in CI/CD Pipelines
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Ansible) in CI/CD Pipelines"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Integrating Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools like Terraform and Ansible into a CI/CD pipeline enables automated, repeatable, and reliable cloud infrastructure provisioning and configuration management."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Pipeline Architecture Strategy"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Phase 1: Terraform provisions the core infrastructure (VPCs, EC2 instances, Kubernetes clusters)."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Phase 2: Ansible configures the provisioned nodes (installing dependencies, deploying application runtimes, setting security hardening)."},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Example GitLab CI/CD Pipeline Configuration"},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"stages:
  - validate
  - plan
  - apply
  - configure

variables:
  TF_ROOT: "infra/terraform"

terraform_plan:
  stage: plan
  image: hashicorp/terraform:latest
  script:
    - cd $TF_ROOT
    - terraform init
    - terraform plan -out=tfplan
  artifacts:
    name: tfplan
    paths:
      - $TF_ROOT/tfplan

terraform_apply:
  stage: apply
  image: hashicorp/terraform:latest
  script:
    - cd $TF_ROOT
    - terraform apply -input=false tfplan
  dependencies:
    - terraform_plan

ansible_configure:
  stage: configure
  image: alpine:latest
  before_script:
    - apk add --no-cache ansible openssh-client
  script:
    - ansible-playbook -i infra/ansible/inventory.ini infra/ansible/playbook.yml"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Best Practices for Production Pipelines"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"State Management: Always store Terraform state files in a secure, remote backend (such as AWS S3 with DynamoDB state locking)."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Secrets Management: Inject sensitive variables like cloud API keys and SSH private keys using pipeline secret stores (GitLab CI/CD Variables or GitHub Actions Secrets)."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Idempotency: Ensure your Ansible playbooks and Terraform manifests are fully idempotent to prevent unintended infrastructure drift during repeated pipeline runs."}]
